subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add Slack RTS as a bundled Slack-plugin `assistant.search.context` action, and what action-token lifetime, redaction, scope, and visibility contract should govern it?
rationale: The request crosses Slack workspace search, event-scoped token handling, and public message-action API design, so automation should not choose the permanent token/security contract.

options.title: Add narrow RTS support
options.body: Implement a Slack-owned read-only RTS action with ephemeral, redacted, thread/account-bound action-token handling and live Slack proof.

options.title: Defer to external plugin
options.body: Leave bundled Slack unchanged until an external plugin or ClawHub package proves the RTS contract and any missing SDK seam.

options.title: Use legacy search only
options.body: Revive `search.messages` user-token search, accepting that it is not Slack's requested event-token RTS path and needs separate privacy review.

recommendation.title: Add narrow RTS support
recommendation.body: Implement a Slack-owned read-only RTS action with ephemeral, redacted, thread/account-bound action-token handling and live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across Slack assistant lifecycle and the broad Slack action-parity work that overlapped this issue.
